steps.name: QC and normalization of raw counts
caveats: With n=6 per group and only 2 batches, batch effects should be modeled as a covariate, not removed by a blind unsupervised correction, since batch is a nuisance factor balanced by design
steps.context: Raw integer gene-level counts from salmon in counts.csv (12000 genes x 12 samples + gene symbol column), paired with metadata.csv (12 rows: condition, batch). This step establishes that the batch/condition design is balanced (design metadata states this) and produces normalized values for visualization before fitting the DE model.
steps.question: Do the 12 kidney samples (6 treated, 6 control, 2 batches) show acceptable library size distributions, and how do samples cluster with respect to condition and batch prior to modeling?
constraints: Use raw counts as provided; do not pre-normalize before DESeq2's own size-factor estimation
Filter genes with very low counts across samples (e.g. rowSum or CPM-based filter) prior to DE, but keep the filtering criterion explicit and reported
acceptance_criteria: Library size and gene-detection summaries reported per sample
PCA or hierarchical clustering plot colored by condition and shaped/labeled by batch produced from variance-stabilized or log-CPM counts
Cross-tabulation of the 6x6 condition-by-batch design confirmed from metadata.csv
Low-count genes filtered using a documented threshold before downstream DE

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression, treated vs control adjusting for batch
caveats: n=6 per group is modest power; interpret genes near the padj threshold cautiously

If batch and condition were confounded rather than balanced this design would not be identifiable — data context states batches are balanced across condition, but the step should verify this from metadata before fitting
steps.context: 12 kidney samples, 6 treated vs 6 control, two batches each holding both conditions (balanced design per the data context). This balance is what makes ~batch + condition a valid and preferred design over batch-blind approaches (e.g. ComBat) that could remove biological signal correlated with batch by chance.
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control kidney samples when the model explicitly adjusts for the two known processing batches (design ~ batch + condition)?
constraints: Design formula must include both batch and condition terms: ~ batch + condition
Report results for the condition term only (treated vs control), not the batch term, as the primary output
Use apeglm or ashr shrinkage for log2FoldChange reporting alongside raw Wald statistics
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 fit using design formula ~ batch + condition on the filtered raw count matrix
Condition contrast (treated vs control) extracted with independent filtering and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction
Full results table (log2FoldChange, p-value, padj) for all tested genes exported, with counts of genes significant at padj < 0.05
MA plot and volcano plot of the treated-vs-control contrast produced
Batch coefficient effect size reported to confirm batch was contributing variance worth adjusting for

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of treated vs control DE genes
caveats: WikiPathways is a smaller, community-curated set than MSigDB Hallmark/KEGG/Reactome, so enrichment coverage and statistical power will be more limited than a full MSigDB-based analysis
steps.context: Uses the DESeq2 treated-vs-control results table from T2S1. Reference needed: a Homo sapiens pathway gene-set collection. WikiPathways human GMT (HGNC gene symbols, '%'-delimited descriptor format) is present in this environment's reference store and matches the organism (Homo sapiens) of this dataset; it is the only pathway reference available here so no KEGG/Reactome/MSigDB alternative should be assumed.
steps.question: Which biological pathways are enriched among genes differentially expressed between treated and control kidney samples (from the ~batch + condition DESeq2 contrast)?
constraints: Use only the human WikiPathways GMT; do not substitute the mouse or rat WikiPathways files present in the reference store
Parse the GMT by splitting the first field on '%' to recover pathway name and WikiPathways ID as documented
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment run (e.g. over-representation or fgsea rank-based) using significant DE genes (padj < 0.05) or the full ranked gene list (by DESeq2 stat) against WikiPathways human gene sets
Results table of pathway name, WikiPathways ID, enrichment p-value/FDR, gene overlap reported
Top enriched pathways (up to 20) summarized and linked back to the direction of regulation (up in treated vs up in control)
Step explicitly reports if the WikiPathways human GMT reference was unavailable at run time, in which case enrichment is skipped and reported as such rather than substituting a non-human resource

plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with batch correction
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a bulk RNA-seq kidney experiment (12000 genes x 13 columns, first column gene symbol -> 12 samples) with 6 treated vs 6 control and two known processing batches balanced across condition. Because batch is balanced across condition, it can and should be explicitly modeled as a covariate in the differential expression design rather than corrected out with a blind method, preserving the biological contrast while removing batch-driven variance. Plan: (1) QC and normalization of raw counts, confirming library size/sample balance and the batch x condition cross-tab; (2) DESeq2 differential expression with a design of ~batch + condition, extracting the condition contrast; (3) pathway enrichment of the resulting DE gene list against WikiPathways human gene sets, since this is the only pathway reference available for Homo sapiens in this environment. No translational/clinical modalities (drug, safety, PK, immune) are indicated by the research question, so no such steps are added.
